primary_route: Yeast-juice fractionation, chemical add-back and heat-dependent functional reconstitution.

checks.quote: # Proposed Fractionation and Reconstitution Protocol: Testing Whether a Heat-Stable Separable Factor Is Required for Yeast-Juice Fermentative Activity
checks.reason: No proposal to consult prior Methods, supplements or validated protocols and verify detailed-condition transfer before execution.
No active-F spike rescue in the treated inactive matrix to exclude introduced inhibitors; no adequate handling-matched unseparated control.
Full-strength DRB plus native fractions is not a final-composition add-back calculation; equal final volume does not hold R enzyme dose constant when F replaces R volume. No evaporation correction.
Precision targets do not calibrate gas accuracy/leakage or product recovery against standards with failure actions.
Units partly specified, but no blank/time-zero carried-product subtraction and weak/missing/saturated endpoint handling.
Triplicate vessels and two membranes from one batch are not independent source preparations; no power/precision plan.
Integrity validity depends on which arms are biologically inactive rather than an outcome-independent technical rule.
Nonsignificant interaction does not establish equivalent methods for pooling; no CI/multiplicity plan. Replication defect is separately P05.
Unknown factor depletion cannot be measured by nucleotide UV260 disappearance alone.
Pilot ranges given but no lock before separate independent confirmatory data.
Repairs lack refreeze and fresh independent confirmation.
Two marker enzymes and failure of BSA rescue cannot exclude damage to unmeasured fermentative enzymes/all stabilizers.
Both share size-separation biases; proposed ethanol confirmation lacks matrix-recovery validation.
No raw-file/unit linkage and exact versioned analysis/provenance audit.
